messages:
lee: Heads-up — noticed that when we fall back from `rdrw-gpt-large` to `rdrw-gpt-small` we're not getting decision-log entries for the fallback. Makes debugging impossible for those requests. Anyone else seen this?

jordan: I saw a pattern last week, thought it was just a logging flake. Can you paste an example trace id?

lee: trace id: t-2026-03-12-9f3b. Here's the tiny excerpt from the gateway log (sanitized):
```
{"ts":"2026-03-12T09:12:03Z","trace_id":"t-2026-03-12-9f3b","route":"/v1/generate","matched_rule":"premium-cmp","decision":"fallback","target_model":"rdrw-gpt-small","status":"200"}
```
But the decision-logs table has no row for that trace_id.

maya: are we sure decision-logs sampling isn't dropping it? IIRC sampling runs at ingress before we evaluate routing debug traces.

samir: dagger: I pulled config for the decision-logs pipeline just now: `cfg get /pipeline/decision-logs`
output: `{"sampling_rate":0.01,"sample_mode":"uniform","log_ttl_days":7}`

jordan: 1% explains missing rows. But that wouldn't bias against fallbacks specifically, unless the sample happens before the fallback decision is materialized.

lee: exactly — it looks like we sample the request early, and if the system later triggers a fallback (or a route override) we don't emit the final evaluation because the sample gate already dropped the event. So we systematically miss interesting cases (errors, fallbacks, region mismatches).

ops-bot: deploy-bot updated pipeline config 1767432005 by samir: changed sampling_rate -> 0.01 (was 0.02) ; rollout: stable

maya: ugh. storage is tight, latency traces are huge, so ops wanted lower sampling. But we need a better policy: sample-uniform is cheap but hides edge behaviors.

samir: proposal: switch to two-stage sampling: cheap uniform sample at ingress for full traces; plus deterministic "always-log" for any request that triggers non-OK routing decisions (fallback, region-failover, quota-block). Implementation idea: tag events that hit a non-primary decision and force them through the decision-log writer without counting against quota.

jordan: We should also consider making the decision-log emitter run after rule-eval completes. Right now the emitter is synchronous at request start to keep latency bounded. Moving it after eval could add ~2-5ms but would capture final decisions. We need perf numbers.

lee: can we do hybrid: emit a tiny pre-eval breadcrumb (trace id + route candidate) for sampling, and then a final evaluation record for deterministic cases only? That keeps volume low and catches the interesting ones.

maya: sounds reasonable. Also want a console toggle so support can temporarily ramp decision log sample to 100% for customer incidents. Add per-org short-term overrides.

samir: ack. I'll prototype changes:
- move sampling gating to after eval OR
- implement deterministic bypass for fallback/quota errors
- add metrics: dropped_by_sampler, emitted_after_eval, forced_emits

jordan: please add a new trace tag `decision_log_status` with values `sampled_pre_eval|sampled_post_eval|forced` so we can query without guessing.

lee: QA note: when you prototype, simulate 1k requests with forced fallbacks to make sure we aren't double-emitting the same trace id. Use `--dedupe` on writer if necessary.

samir: good call. I'll throw up a small branch and a canary config. Thinking to keep default sampling at 1% but set forced bypass to always pass. Also add a TTL ramp for forced events — 30d by default.

maya: can we also add a small UI card that says "Decision log sampling: 1% (forced bypass for fallbacks)" in the route debug panel? helps support know why some traces exist.

ops-bot: plan created: PL-1773 decision-log deterministic bypass + UI toggle. Assignee: samir. Severity: medium. ETA: end of sprint.

jordan: I'll run a perf bench when samir has a branch. If post-eval emission adds >5ms p50 we'll prefer the bypass path.

lee: thanks folks. For follow-up, can we also surface how many fallbacks happen per route in the route dashboard? That would have alerted us earlier.

maya: +1. I'll add a feature request to the console board.

samir: starting work today, will drop a PR and ping here when ready for canary.

lee: perfect. :thumbsup:

jordan: thanks — looping in support lead if we need a temporary sample bump during customer debug. @maya can you coordinate?

maya: yep, will coordinate with support to enable a 100% sample window if needed.

ops-bot: support-runbook link: https://internal/redwood/runbooks/decision-log-debugging

lee: awesome. closing thread for now, will reopen if PR causes ripples.
